clue.text: Extravagantly dine on things: this could just go on and on

definitions.text: this could just go on and on

indicators.note: doing something extravagantly means wildly, without restraint, so the three words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A lavish diner eats without stopping, a meal that seems to go on for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extravagantly' rearranges DINEONTHINGS into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation with no end in sight is one whose finish cannot be seen, so it seems set to continue indefinitely.

clue.text: Old prison with freshly made entranceway

parts.note: something freshly made is new
a gate is an entranceway

explanation.surface: An old jail boasts a newly built entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWGATE was a notorious London prison, demolished in 1904.
explanation.definitionFit: Newgate was a historic London jail, so it is literally an old prison.

clue.text: Stye, perhaps? That doesn't look good

definitions.meaning: a stye is a sore on the eyelid

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a stye in the mirror and decides it does not look good.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into EYE SORE; the question mark flags a stye as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, while an eyesore is anything unsightly.

clue.text: Unfortunately, lie: and I'd lose this source of energy

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so these letters are knocked into a different order

explanation.surface: A confession: telling a lie would cost someone the energy supply they rely on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' rearranges LIEIDLOSE; 'and' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel oil is fuel burned in engines and generators, so a source of power.

clue.text: Titles shown in Vietnamese

indicators.note: the answer is shown inside the single word that follows, sitting within its letters

explanation.surface: A book's titles are displayed in the Vietnamese language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown in' points to the letters inside VietNAMESe.
explanation.definitionFit: Titles are what things are called, which is what names are.

clue.text: Fashionable princess in a state?

parts.note: something fashionable is in
Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A stylish princess finds herself in a state of agitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' reads as being flustered; 'state' alone is the definition, an American one.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty United States, so an example of a state.

clue.text: Looking for a get out? Harry's your man!

definitions.text: Looking for a get out? Harry's your man!

parts.words: Looking for a get out? Harry's your man!
parts.note: the famous escapologist named Harry is the man to ask about getting out of anything

explanation.surface: An advert recommends a fixer called Harry for anyone needing an escape route.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Houdini was the celebrated escape artist who freed himself from chains, locks and tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Houdini made his name escaping from restraints, so he is the man for a getaway.

clue.text: Confusion, as gentlemen tan badly

indicators.note: done badly means messed up, so these letters are jumbled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Chaos ensues as gentlemen sunbathe and burn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges GENTLEMENTAN; 'as' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An entanglement is a muddle or complicated tangle, a state of confusion.

clue.text: At this time, in this location, it's not the place to be

parts.note: at this time means now
in this location means here

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the spot they are in right now is not where they want to be.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works as a cryptic hint: nowhere is literally no place at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowhere means no place, so it is not any place where one could be.

clue.text: Late to get in touch with these people?

definitions.text: Late to get in touch with these people?

parts.words: Late to get in touch with these people?
parts.note: the late here are the dead, and these people claim to contact them

explanation.surface: It reads like someone running behind schedule before meeting some people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' looks like tardiness but means the deceased, whom spiritualists claim to reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediums are spiritualists who claim to pass messages from the dead to the living.

clue.text: Task gig's crew to shift what officer might carry

indicators.note: to shift is to move things about, so these letters change places

explanation.surface: A band's road crew is told to move the gear, including something an officer carries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to shift' rearranges TASKGIGSCREW.
explanation.definitionFit: A swagger stick is a short cane carried by military officers as a mark of rank.

clue.text: Sailor with a solitary decorative shell

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
solitary means lone

explanation.surface: A lonely sailor owns a single ornamental shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone is a sea snail whose iridescent shell is used for mother-of-pearl ornaments.

clue.text: Just a minaret, embodying something that keeps you going?

indicators.note: the phrase is said to embody the answer, holding it within its run of letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a mere minaret could be a source of endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embodying' points to the letters inside juST A MINAret.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the endurance that lets someone keep on going.

clue.text: Obese egrets holding other birds back

indicators.note: back means the hidden run is read from right to left
the two words hold the answer within their joined letters

explanation.surface: Fat herons are holding back a flock of different birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' finds ESEEG inside obESE EGrets; 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Geese are waterfowl, birds of a different kind from the egrets in the clue.

clue.text: Working — in the theatre?

definitions.meaning: a machine that is ... is working
a surgeon ... is at work in the ... theatre

explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests the stage, but it is the hospital operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Operating means functioning, and also performing surgery, which happens in a theatre.

clue.text: Founders of the original pyramid scheme?

definitions.text: Founders of the original pyramid scheme?

parts.words: Founders of the original pyramid scheme?
parts.note: a pyramid scheme is a financial fraud, but taken literally the first scheme for pyramids was ancient

explanation.surface: It sounds like a question about who invented a notorious financial fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pyramid scheme' means a fraud, but here it is the building of the actual pyramids.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient people of the Nile built the first great pyramids at Giza.

clue.text: On the outside, with no kiss, forever

indicators.note: with no means the kiss is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: on the outside means externally
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone left outside without so much as a kiss feels it will last for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally means for all time, without end.

clue.text: Cook gutted hen later, in hold

indicators.note: to cook something is to fiddle with it, so these letters are rearranged
a gutted word has lost its insides, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction: prepare the cleaned hen afterwards, keeping it in the hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' leaves HN of hen; 'Cook' rearranges HN plus LATER. 'in' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral is to captivate, to hold someone's attention spellbound.

clue.text: Ewan, initially in close proximity to Edward, mimicked a horse?

indicators.note: in means that letter goes inside the word for nearness

parts.note: nigh means near, in close proximity

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the name is used

parts.note: Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Ewan, standing close to Edward, does an impression of a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts E inside NIGH to make NEIGH; 'to' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's cry is a neigh, so imitating one means making that sound.

clue.text: Scrooge bound by promise, repents

indicators.note: the answer is bound inside the two words, enclosed across their join

explanation.surface: Scrooge, held to a promise, has a change of heart, as in A Christmas Carol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound by' finds the letters inside proMISE Repents.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer Scrooge is the archetypal skinflint, so his name stands for any miser.

clue.text: Mother's lip on first half of bass instrument

parts.note: ma is a word for mother
a lip is a rim or edge

indicators.note: the first half of the word means its opening two letters

explanation.surface: Mum's mouth rests on part of a bass instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' only joins the pieces, MA then RIM then BA.
explanation.definitionFit: A marimba is a percussion instrument with wooden bars, like a large xylophone.

clue.text: After entertaining the French, not a peep

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest, so one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: since means after, as in 'since the war'
le is French for the

explanation.surface: After hosting some French visitors, there is not a sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is the outer piece, not a placement instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Silence is the absence of sound, not even a peep.

clue.text: Merge hospital department with Bordeaux, possibly

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
Bordeaux is an example of wine

explanation.surface: A hospital unit combines with a French wine region, perhaps in a merger.
explanation.definitionFit: To entwine is to twist together, joining things into one.

clue.text: Ascetic ultimately leaves German city

indicators.note: ultimately leaves means the last letter goes away

parts.note: the Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect, so an Essene is an ascetic

explanation.surface: A hermit eventually departs for a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr, in western Germany.

clue.text: Pastry later baked in test of speed?

indicators.note: in means the reworked letters sit inside the other piece

parts.note: TT, the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man, is a test of speed

indicators.note: baked means cooked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cake-making contest: pastry baked afterwards in a timed trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'test of speed' is the Isle of Man TT motorcycle race, not a baking challenge; 'baked' signals the rearrangement and 'in' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartlet is a small tart, a pastry case with a filling.

clue.text: Sets fire to last of walnut or half of chestnut

indicators.note: the last of the word means its final letter
half of the word means its first four letters

explanation.surface: Someone lights a fire from walnut or chestnut wood.
explanation.definitionFit: To torch something is to set it alight deliberately.

clue.text: Alan: chap with a century calendar

parts.note: Al is short for Alan
a chap is a man
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: Alan, a fellow who owns a hundred-year calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alan' is cut to AL; 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a yearly publication listing dates, events and astronomical data, a kind of calendar.

clue.text: On which one might rank the best skaters?

definitions.text: On which one might rank the best skaters?

parts.words: On which one might rank the best skaters?
parts.note: skaters glide along the ice, so a gliding measure of ranking fits them literally

explanation.surface: It asks what system judges would use to rank top skaters.
explanation.walkthrough: A sliding scale is a variable rate; skaters, taken literally, slide.
explanation.definitionFit: A sliding scale is a graded scale of values that varies with conditions, used for ranking or charging.
